question: Which country in West Africa has the highest total population?
explanation: Spot on! Nigeria is the most populous nation in Africa and drives a lot of the demographic growth in our region. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h1)

question: Why do nursing students learn about population birth trends?

options.A: To calculate national financial budgets for the government
options.B: To accurately predict community maternal and child healthcare needs
options.C: To determine international trade policies for medical goods
options.D: To replace the work of civil registrars and census officers

explanation: You got it! Knowing birth rates helps you anticipate how many mothers and babies will need care in your facility. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h1)

question: What does 'Total Fertility Rate' (TFR) actually measure?

options.A: The percentage of women using modern family planning methods
options.B: The average number of children a woman has during her reproductive years
options.C: The average age of mothers when giving birth to their first child
options.D: The total number of children born in a single hospital annually

explanation: Exactly! TFR estimates the average number of children a woman is expected to have throughout her childbearing years. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h2)

question: What is a major result of a country having a high birth rate over many years?

options.A: A heavy economic dependency ratio with many young citizens
options.B: A rapid increase in the average age of the working population
options.C: An immediate shortage of geriatric care facilities
options.D: A permanent surplus of maternal hospital beds nationwide

explanation: Correct! High birth rates create a young population, meaning fewer working adults have to support many children. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h2)

question: Why do many rural families traditionally view having many children as a great benefit?

options.A: The government pays monthly stipends for large households
options.B: Children provide farm labor and security in old age
options.C: Larger households receive free agricultural land allotments
options.D: School fees are fully subsidized for families with five children

explanation: Spot on! In farming communities, children help out on the farm and support their parents as they grow older. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h3)

question: How does wanting a male child (son preference) affect family sizes in some communities?

options.A: It drives couples to keep trying for a boy, increasing total births
options.B: It has no statistical influence on community birth patterns
options.C: It automatically lowers the median age of marriage for women
options.D: It encourages families to stop childbearing after the first daughter

explanation: You're right! When families really want a baby boy, they often keep having children past their original goal until a son arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h3)

question: In Nigeria, which setting usually records the lowest fertility rates?
explanation: Correct! City dwellers often have smaller family sizes due to higher living costs and better access to school and family planning. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h4)

question: How does keeping girls in school longer usually affect their age at marriage?

options.A: It forces marriage at an earlier age
options.B: It has no effect on marriage timing
options.C: It prevents women from ever marrying
options.D: It delays marriage to a later age

explanation: Exactly! Education keeps young women in school, which naturally pushes their age of first marriage higher. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h5)

question: Why does empowering women often lead to smaller, more planned families?

options.A: Employers legally restrict female workers from starting families
options.B: Women lose their biological capacity to conceive after higher education
options.C: Women gain greater decision-making power over their reproductive health
options.D: Government laws force educated women to have fewer children

explanation: Spot on! When women are empowered, they have a stronger voice in deciding family size and birth spacing. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h5)

question: What is a common myth that scares many Nigerian women away from using modern birth control?

options.A: Fear of permanent infertility or severe side effects
options.B: Idea that injections cause immediate hair loss
options.C: Belief that birth control methods are free of charge
options.D: Assumption that pills increase visual acuity

explanation: Correct! Worries about permanent barrenness or scary side effects are major barriers we encounter in community practice. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do when promoting family planning?

options.A: Ensuring client confidentiality during health consultations
options.B: Dispelling common myths regarding modern contraceptive safety
options.C: Providing accurate counseling on various birth control options
options.D: Forcing community members to adopt specific contraceptive devices

explanation: You got it! Family planning must always be a personal choice. Forcing anyone goes against nursing ethics and human rights. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h6)

question: How do high birth rates directly impact hospital maternity wards in busy areas?

options.A: They create an excess of sterile delivery equipment
options.B: They decrease the need for newborn immunization supplies
options.C: They cause severe overcrowding and strain available nursing staff
options.D: They eliminate the occurrence of postpartum complications

explanation: Spot on! Too many deliveries at once stretch hospital beds and overworked nurses to their limits. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h7)

question: You are posted to a rural village where women have closely spaced pregnancies. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise community leaders to ban all marriages for young women
options.B: Wait for patients to visit the hospital before discussing reproductive health
options.C: Organize community education on birth spacing and offer family planning counseling
options.D: Focus all clinic resources exclusively on geriatric care programs

explanation: Fantastic! Taking education directly to the community helps families learn about safe birth spacing and maternal health. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h7)
